name: Crowdie Oatcakes
desc: Crowdie, the soft, crumbly Highland cheese, spread thick on oatcakes. Restores 110 HP and a sense of being well fed.

name: Partan Bree
desc: Partan is Scots for crab and bree is broth: a rich, creamy crab soup from the north-east coast. Restores 170 HP.

name: Groatie Buckie
desc: A tiny pink cowrie shell from the beach at John o' Groats. Rare, ribbed and famously lucky.
msg: {name}'s Groatie Buckie brought a bit of luck!

name: Bog Myrtle Sprig
desc: A sprig of sweet gale from the Flow Country. Rub the leaves and the midges keep away, mostly. It once flavoured beer.
msg: {name}'s Bog Myrtle took the sting out of it!

name: Burn Water Flask
desc: Fresh water from a Caithness burn, corked in a flask. Orkney lore says the Nuckelavee cannot cross running fresh water.
msg: {name}'s Burn Water Flask kept the sea at bay!

name: Caithness Flagstone
desc: A thin, tough slab of Old Red Sandstone that splits as flat as a table. Caithness built its houses, roofs and fences from it.

name: End to End Card
desc: A card for the journey from John o' Groats to Land's End, 874 miles by the signpost. Stamp it at both ends.

name: End to End Certificate
desc: Official proof you have been to both ends of Britain. There's a drawing of the signpost at the top and a pasty crumb in the corner.

name: Tide Tables
desc: The Tide Watcher's own tables for the Pentland Firth, pencilled with warnings like 'NO' and 'REALLY NO'.
